# Spergularia flaccida (Madden) I.M.Turner

First published in Willdenowia 47: 214 (2017)

This species is accepted

The native range of this species is Macaronesia, N. Africa to Mauritania, Sicilia (Linosa) to NW. India and NE. Tropical Africa. It is an annual and grows primarily in the desert or dry shrubland biome.

### According to Flora of Iraq under the synonym Spergula fallax

Ghazanfar, S. A. & Edmondson, J. R (Eds). (2016) Flora of Iraq, Volume 5 Part 1: Elatinaceae to Sphenocleaceae.

Morphology General Habit
    Annual herbs
Morphology Stem
    Stems 5–40 cm, with ascending stems ± branched at the base, glabrous throughout
Morphology Leaves
    Leaves 1–3.5 cm, linear, fleshy, not canaliculated beneath
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Calyx
    Sepals 3–5 mm, oblong-lanceolate
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Corolla
    Petals white, equalling or somewhat shorter than the sepals
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Androecium Stamens
    Stamens 10, rarely less
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Gynoecium Style
    Styles 3
Morphology Reproductive morphology Fruits
    Capsule 4–5 mm, somewhat exceeding the sepals, dehiscing by 3 valves
Morphology Reproductive morphology Seeds
    Seeds 0.8–1 mm (excluding wing), compressed, grey-black, encircled by a broad scarious wing.
Ecology
    Sandy soil in wadis, alluvial flats, roadsides, fields etc. alt. 5–550 m;
Phenology
    Flowering & fruiting: Feb.–May.
Distribution
    Widespread in the deserts and lowlands of Iraq. Madeira, Canary Is., N Africa, SW Asia, NW and C India.
[FIQ]

### According to Flora of Somalia under the synonym Spergula fallax

M. Thulin et al. Flora of Somalia, Vol. 1-4 [updated 2008] https://plants.jstor.org/collection/FLOS

Morphology General Habit
    Erect or ascending annual herb, to 25 cm high, most parts glabrous or nearly so
Morphology Leaves
    Leaves densely clustered at nodes, linear, to 25 x c. 0.5 mm, tip acute; stipules triangular-ovate, soon falling
Morphology Reproductive morphology Inflorescences
    Cymes lax, dichasial; peduncles up to 20–30 mm
Morphology Reproductive morphology Inflorescences Bracts
    Bracts scarious, c. 1.5 mm long
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Calyx
    Sepals ovate-elliptic, c. 3.5 mm long, subacute to obtuse
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Corolla
    Petals ovate, slightly shorter than sepals
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Androecium Stamens
    Stamens (6–)10, shorter than ovary
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Gynoecium Style
    Styles 3
Morphology Reproductive morphology Fruits
    Capsule slightly longer than sepals
Morphology Reproductive morphology Seeds
    Seeds black with broadly winged whitish margin, c. 1.1 mm in diam.
Distribution
    N3 (Galgala) North Africa west to Atlantic Is., east to Iran, Afghanistan and India, Sudan.
Ecology
    Altitude c. 1150 m.
[FSOM]
